chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from Abī ‘Abdillāh al-Mu’min, from Ibn Muskān, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: Verily, for Allah there are one hundred thousand glances (moments) every day and night towards the earth, through which He forgives whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills. And He specifically forgives those who perform Ziyārah to the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), and their family members, and those for whom they will intercede on the Day of Resurrection, regardless of who they may be, even if they are a man upon whom Hell has been made obligatory. I asked: 'Even if he is a man upon whom Hell has been made obligatory?' He replied: 'Yes, as long as he is not a Nāṣibī.'

key_terms.اسْتَوْجَبَهُ النَّارُ: Upon whom Hell has been made obligatory; those destined for Hellfire due to their sins.
key_terms.زَائِرِي قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Visitors to the grave of al-Husayn; those performing Ziyārah.
key_terms.لَحْظَةٍ: A glance or moment; a brief instant of divine attention.
key_terms.نَاصِبِيًّا: Nāṣibī; one who is hostile or envious towards the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly the Imams.
key_terms.يَشْفَعُ لَهُمْ: Intercede for them; the power to advocate on behalf of others on the Day of Judgment.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ziyārah to the grave of Imam al-Husain regarding intercession and forgiveness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarah* highlights the cosmic scale of divine mercy, noting that Allah has 100,000 moments of forgiveness daily, with a special emphasis on visitors of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). It introduces the profound Shia concept of *Shafa'ah* (intercession), asserting that even those who have earned Hellfire may be saved through the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt, provided they are not *Nāṣibī* (enemies of the Imams). This underscores the pivotal role of Ziyarah in securing salvation and divine favor in Shia eschatology.
